title: BF16/INT8 NaN trace - scratchbook
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal log for tracking a recurring NaN/quality regression that shows up when running models in BF16 with INT8 quantized weights. This is a scratchpad: commands, outputs, hypotheses, short tracebacks, quick tests to run next. Not polished.

Incident summary (high level):
- Observed NaNs during generation (sometimes in logits, sometimes in attention scores) in runtime that supports mixed BF16/INT8 paths.
- Repro rate ~ 12% on full workload; higher (~60%) when sequence length > 1024 or with heavy KV-cache reuse (long chitchat sessions).
- Happens after ~3-10 tokens into generation for some prompts.

Quick repro (local) - what I ran:
1) Exported the model variant with INT8 weight files and BF16 activation pipeline.
2) Run single-node test invocation (local GPU, CUDA 12.x):

python -m torch.distributed.run --nproc_per_node=1 tests/run_generation.py \
  --model-path ./exported/int8-bf16/model.pt \
  --dtype bf16 --use-quant int8 --max-new-tokens 128 \
  --prompt-file repro/prompts.txt --seed 42 --log-every 1

Observed stdout snippet (abridged):
[2024-11-01 14:33:02] INFO: loading model -> ./exported/int8-bf16/model.pt
[2024-11-01 14:33:12] WARN: detected unstable-softmax: max logits > 1e4, applying safety-scale
[2024-11-01 14:33:13] ERROR: generation loop: encountered NaN in logits at step 5
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "tests/run_generation.py", line 142, in <module>
    out = model.generate(input_ids, max_new_tokens=args.max_new_tokens)
  File "./runtime/inference.py", line 381, in generate
    logits = self.forward_step(inputs)
  File "./runtime/inference.py", line 210, in forward_step
    attn = self.attention(query, key, value)
  File "./runtime/ops/attention.py", line 77, in attention
    attn_scores = (query @ key.transpose(-2, -1)) * scale
  File "<built-in>", line 0, in _th_kernel
RuntimeError: CUDA error: device-side assert triggered (NaN encountered)

Quick log probes I added:
- Inserted an assert after matmul: if torch.isnan(attn_scores).any(): print(layer_idx, torch.isnan(attn_scores).nonzero()[:10])
- Logged max/min of weights after dequantization, and the per-channel scale used by quantizer.

What the quick probes showed (abbreviated):
- NaNs appear first in attn_scores, not in queries or keys individually (both finite).
- Per-channel scales: one outlier channel in layer 8 has scale ~1e-7 (tiny) while most are ~0.02-0.5. Dequantized weights for that channel have very large values (~1e5) after scaling.
- The quantizer is asymmetric per-channel int8 with zero-point; code path does dequantize: float_w = (int8_w - zp) * scale. If scale is tiny but int8 values near -128, result can be large negative/positive.

Hypothesis 1 (weight calibration artifact):
- The calibration step produced near-zero scale for a few channels because the channel had very small dynamic range in calibration data. During actual inference, activation distribution differs, leading to large effective weights after dequantize (due to underflow/overfitting of scale). That blows up attention scores -> NaN.
- Supporting evidence: outlier per-channel scale found in probe.

Hypothesis 2 (BF16 accumulation overflow):
- MatMul accumulation uses BF16 accumulation path (faster kernels) in our runtime. If dequantized weights have extreme magnitudes in a channel, BF16 accumulation loses precision and saturates to Inf/NaN when exponent overflows.
- Repro pattern: happens more at longer seq lengths (more summation, larger intermediate sums).

Hypothesis 3 (KV-cache replay + stale quant params):
- When KV-cache is reused across calls, we may be reusing cached dequantized keys that were produced under one set of calibration params, but models swapped to different quant params (rare path in dedicated/dynamic routing). Cached values not invalidated -> mismatch -> NaN.
- Repro increase with long sessions supports cache involvement.

Quick tests I ran to differentiate:
A) Force FP32 dequantization path locally: dequant = int8_w.float() * scale (cast to float32) and use FP32 matmul. Repro rate -> 0% in ~100 runs.
B) Clamp scales minimum to 1e-3 during dequant -> repro rate drops to ~2%.
C) Disable KV cache -> repro rate drops to <5% for same prompt set.
D) Run with full FP16 activations instead of BF16 -> repro disappears.

Notes from A/B/C/D:
- A suggests precision/accumulation matters. B suggests bad small scales are correlated. C implicates KV cache or its lifecycle. D suggests BF16 accumulation loss is a factor. Probably interplay of all three.

Edge-case traces I captured (raw-ish):
- layer 8, head 3, token-step 5 -> attn_scores[0,3,4] = NaN; query max= 3.2, key max=4.1, dequantized weight max = 1.2e5 for channel 3.
- scale for channel 3 = 6.8e-8; zero_point = -12.

Short mitigation patch tried (local):
- In quantizer post-calibration, enforce min_scale = max(min_scale, 1e-4) and recompute dequantized weights. Pack model and run. Result: Repro goes way down.
- Concern: min_scale clamp may degrade final model quality if channel truly requires small scale (rare). Need measured eval.

Checklist / Next reproducibility steps (ordered):
1) Create small synthetic test that isolates single channel: craft input that activates channel 3 strongly (use logits from FP32 model to guide). Run with INT8 dequant and BF16 accumulation to get deterministic failure.
2) Add unit test to runtime for cached-key invalidation when model quant params change.
3) Instrument quantization pipeline to dump per-channel histograms before/after calibration for every model upload.
4) Run long-seq stress tests with and without KV cache to collect failure rate and minimal reproducible prompt.
5) Try disabling BF16 accumulation only for the layer with outlier scales (fallback to FP32/FP16 accumulation) as a mitigation.

Longer-term fixes to evaluate:
- Switch to per-channel min_scale clamp policy based on historical activation distribution rather than absolute floor.
- During model import, run a small set of random inputs to validate that dequantized weights don't produce extreme values when used with BF16 kernels. Reject and flag models that fail; surface to model-onboarding.
- Improve cache metadata: store quantization fingerprint with KV blocks; validate on reuse. If mismatch, re-dequantize or invalidate.
- Prefer FP32/FP16 accum for layers with high dynamic range or per-channel scale outliers.

Quick todo for next day: (short actionable)
- [ ] Implement synthetic isolation test for channel-level activation (1 hr) - Evan
- [ ] Add min-scale clamp flag behind runtime config and run nightly evaluation on small dev cluster (Samir)
- [ ] Add quant-fingerprint into KV cache header (Priya)
- [ ] Run evaluation job comparing clamp vs no-clamp on eval set (Priya/Evan)

Notes to self:
- Keep sample logs and per-channel scales for at least 7 days in diagnostics bucket to correlate with customer incidents.
- If we ship min-scale clamp, create an eval that measures perplexity/regression < 0.5% on held-out set; otherwise need safer approach.

Possible false leads I ruled out quickly:
- CUDA driver bug: tried on two different GPUs (A100 + H100), same behavior on both.
- Model corruption on disk: checksum verified before run.
- Bad random seed: fixed seed and still repro.

Misc commands & snippets saved here for future copy-paste:
- dump per-channel scales from quant metadata:
python tools/inspect_quant.py --model export/model -o output/scales.json

- quick dequant probe (python):
import torch
meta = load_quant_meta('export/model')
int8_w = torch.frombuffer(..., dtype=torch.int8)
scale = torch.tensor(meta['scales'])
zp = torch.tensor(meta['zero_points'])
float_w = (int8_w.to(torch.float32) - zp.view(-1,1)) * scale.view(-1,1) # force fp32
print(float_w[channel].abs().max())

- flag to runtime to force FP32 accumulation (env): RUNTIME_ACCUM_MODE=fp32 python ...

Random thoughts:
- Could use a small calibration dataset that includes longer sequences so channels with rare but large activation patterns don't collapse to tiny scales.
- We should ask model-onboarding whether training used LayerNorm variants that produce extremely skewed distributions for certain channels.

If anyone else reads this and has pointers: send short note with "bf16-int8-nan" in slack and drop pointer to reproducer.

Evan
